answer: Post-hoc timing correlation audit clusters accounts by pairwise action-time alignment against a null model. It flags cohorts whose intervals correlate above threshold and holds payouts for revalidation. Detection is calibrated with opal, a held-out set of independent accounts. Evasion requires each identity to inject a zephyr of independent timing noise. The timing signal is evaluated after the fact. Each identity pays separate compute, scheduling, and coordination overhead, multiplying attacker cost.
